definitions.explanation: Calling out names or numbers to check attendance, typically in military, school, workplace, or emergency contexts.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}の{点呼|てんこ}が{始|はじ}まった。
{避難|ひなん}{後|ご}、{全員|ぜんいん}の{点呼|てんこ}をとった。
examples.english: After the evacuation, a head count of everyone was taken.

examples.japanese: バスの{運転手|うんてんしゅ}は{出発前|しゅっぱつまえ}に{乗客|じょうきゃく}の{点呼|てんこ}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: The bus driver conducted a roll call of passengers before departure.

notes:
Compound of {点|てん} (point/check) + {呼|こ} (call). The act of calling names or numbers to verify attendance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {点呼|てんこ}をとる: to take roll call
- {点呼|てんこ}する: to do a roll call
- {点呼|てんこ}を{行|おこな}う: to conduct a roll call (formal)
- {朝|あさ}の{点呼|てんこ}: morning roll call

CONTEXTS:
Used in settings where attendance verification is important:
- {軍隊|ぐんたい}: military
- {学校|がっこう}: school (especially field trips, evacuations)
- {避難|ひなん}{訓練|くんれん}: evacuation drills
- {工事|こうじ}{現場|げんば}: construction sites

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {出欠|しゅっけつ}をとる: to take attendance (classroom setting, more everyday)
- {人数|にんずう}{確認|かくにん}: headcount/confirmation of numbers
